**Core Variables v3.5**

**OpenSIPS** provides multiple type of variables to be used in the routing script. The difference between the types of variables comes from (1) the visibility of the variable (when it is visible), (2) what the variable is attached to (where the variable resides), (3) read-write status of the variable (some types of the variables are read-only and (4) how multiple values (for the same variable are handled).

The **OpenSIPS** variables can be easily identified in the script as all their names (or notations) start with the **$** sign.

Syntax:
The complete syntax for a pseudo variable is:

$(_<context>_**name**_(subname)[index]{transformation}_)

The fields written in green are optional. The fields meaning is:

*   **name**(compulsory) - the pseudo-variable name(type).
    Ex: pvar, avp, ru, DLG_status, etc.
*   **subname** - the identifier of a certain pv from the given type.
    Ex: hdr(From), avp(name).
*   **index** - a pv can store more than one value - it can refer to a list of values. You can access a certain value from the list if you specify its index. You can also specify indexes with negative values, -1 means the last inserted, -2 the value before the previous inserted one.
*   **transformation** - a series of processing actions can be applied on pseudo-variable. You can find the whole list of possible transformations here. The transformations can be cascaded, using the output of one transformation as the input of another.
*   **context** - the context in which the pseudo0variable will be evaluated. Now there are 2 pv contexts: reply and request. The reply context can be used in the failure route to request for the pseudo-variable to be evaluated in the context of the reply message. The request context can be used if in a reply route is desired for the pv to be evaluated in the context of the corresponding request.

Usage examples:

*   Only **name**: $ru
*   **Name** and _'subname_: $hdr(Contact)
*   **Name** and **index**: $(ct[0])
*   **Name**, **subname** and **index**: $(avp(i:10)[2])
*   **Context**
    *   $(<request>ru) from a reply route will get the Request-URI from the request
    *   $(<reply>hdr(Contact)) context can be used from failure route to access information from the reply

Types of variables:

*   **script variables** - as the name says, these variables are strictly bound to the script routes. The variables are visible only in the routing blocks - they are not message or transaction related, but they are process related (script variables will be inherited by script routes executed by the same **OpenSIPS** process).
    Script variables are read write and they can have integer or string values. A script variable can only hold a single value. A new assignment (or write operation) will overwrite the existing value.
    
*   **AVP - Attribute Value Pair** - the AVPs are dynamic variables (as name) that can be created - the AVPS are linked to a singular message or transaction (if stateful processing is used). A message or a transaction will initially (when received or created) have an empty list of AVPS attached to it. During the routing script, the script directly or functions called from script may create new AVPS that will automatically attached to the message/transaction. The AVPS will be visible in all routes where any message (reply or request) of the transaction will be processed - branch_route , failure_route, onreply_route (for this last route you need to enable the TM parameter _onreply_avp_mode_).
    AVPs are read write and an existing AVP can be even deleted (removed). An AVP may contain multiple values - a new assignment (or write operation) will add a new value to the AVP; the values are kept in "last added first to be used" order (stack).
    A special index **append** is defined to allow you to add a new value at the end of the list (at the bottom of the stack) - $(avp(name)[append]) = "last value";
    
*   **pseudo variables** - pseudo-variables (or PV) provide access to information from the processed SIP message (headers, RURI, transport level info, a.s.o) or from **OpenSIPS** inners (time values, process PID, return code of a function). Depending of what info they provide, the PVs are either bound to the message, either to nothing (global). Most of the PVs are read-only and only several allow write operations. A PV may return several values or only one, depending of the referred info (if can have multiple values or not).
    Standard PV is read-only and returns a single value (if not otherwise documented).
    
*   **escape sequences** - escape sequences used to format the strings; they are actually not variables, but rather formatters.

variables.name: $var(name)
variables.description: Script variables strictly bound to the script routes. Visible only in the routing blocks - they are not message or transaction related, but they are process related.

variables.name: $avp(name)
variables.description: Attribute Value Pair - dynamic variables linked to a singular message or transaction.

variables.name: $ai
variables.description: reference to URI in request's P-Asserted-Identity header (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $adu
variables.description: URI from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header. This URI is used when calculating the HTTP Digest Response.

variables.name: $ar
variables.description: realm from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $au
variables.description: user part of username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $ad
variables.description: domain part of username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $an
variables.description: the nonce from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.resp
variables.description: the authentication response from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.nonce
variables.description: the nonce string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.opaque
variables.description: the opaque string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.alg
variables.description: the algorithm string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.qop
variables.description: the value of qop parameter from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.nc
variables.description: the value of nonce count parameter from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $aU
variables.description: whole username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $Au
variables.description: username for accounting purposes. It's a selective pseudo variable (inherited from acc module). It returns $au if exits or From username otherwise.

variables.name: $argv
variables.description: provides access to command line arguments specified with '-o' option.

variables.name: $bf
variables.description: displays a list with the branch flags set for the current SIP request

variables.name: $branch
variables.description: this variable is used for creating new branches by writing into it the value of a SIP URI.

variables.name: $branch()
variables.description: this variable provides read/write access to all fields/attributes of an already existing branch (prior created with append_branch() ).

subfields.name: uri
subfields.description: the RURI of the branch

subfields.name: duri
subfields.description: destination URI of the branch (outbound proxy of the branch)

subfields.name: q
subfields.description: q value of the branch

subfields.name: path
subfields.description: the PATH string for this branch

subfields.name: flags
subfields.description: the branch flags of this branch

subfields.name: socket
subfields.description: the local socket to be used for relaying this branch

variables.name: $branch.flag()
variables.description: this variable provides read/write access to the value of a single certain branch flag (identified by name).

variables.name: $ci
variables.description: reference to body of call-id header

variables.name: $cl
variables.description: reference to body of content-length header

variables.name: $cs
variables.description: reference to cseq number from cseq header

variables.name: $ct
variables.description: reference to contact instance/body from the contact header. A contact instance is display_name + URI + contact_params.

variables.name: $ct.fields()
variables.description: reference to the fields of a contact instance/body

subfields.name: name
subfields.description: display name

subfields.name: uri
subfields.description: contact uri

subfields.name: q
subfields.description: q param (value only)

subfields.name: expires
subfields.description: expires param (value only)

subfields.name: methods
subfields.description: methods param (value only)

subfields.name: received
subfields.description: received param (value only)

subfields.name: params
subfields.description: all params (including names)

variables.name: $cT
variables.description: reference to body of Content-Type header and also the content-type headers inside a multi-part body

variables.name: $dd
variables.description: reference to domain of destination uri

variables.name: $di
variables.description: reference to Diversion header URI

variables.name: $dip
variables.description: reference to Diversion header "privacy" parameter value

variables.name: $dir
variables.description: reference to Diversion header "reason" parameter value

variables.name: $dp
variables.description: reference to port of destination uri

variables.name: $dP
variables.description: reference to transport protocol of destination uri

variables.name: $ds
variables.description: reference to destination set

variables.name: $du
variables.description: reference to destination uri (outbound proxy to be used for sending the request)

variables.name: $err.class
variables.description: the class of error (now is '1' for parsing errors)

variables.name: $err.level
variables.description: severity level for the error

variables.name: $err.info
variables.description: text describing the error

variables.name: $err.rcode
variables.description: recommended reply code

variables.name: $err.rreason
variables.description: recommended reply reason phrase

variables.name: $fd
variables.description: reference to domain in URI of 'From' header

variables.name: $fn
variables.description: reference to display name of 'From' header

variables.name: $ft
variables.description: reference to tag parameter of 'From' header

variables.name: $fu
variables.description: reference to URI of 'From' header

variables.name: $fU
variables.description: reference to username in URI of 'From' header

variables.name: $log_level
variables.description: changes the log level for the current process

variables.name: $mb
variables.description: reference to SIP message buffer

variables.name: $mf
variables.description: displays a list with the message/transaction flags set for the current SIP request

variables.name: $mi
variables.description: reference to SIP message id

variables.name: $ml
variables.description: reference to SIP message length

variables.name: $msg.flag()
variables.description: this variable provides read/write access to the value of a single certain message flag (identified by name).

variables.name: $msg.is_request
variables.description: this variable tells if the current SIP message is a request or not.

examples.description: Checking if message is a request

variables.name: $msg.type
variables.description: this variable returns the type of the current message. The returned values are "request" (request) or "reply" (reply).

examples.code: xlog("---- this message is a SIP $msg.type \n");

variables.name: $od
variables.description: reference to domain in request's original R-URI

variables.name: $op
variables.description: reference to port of original R-URI

variables.name: $oP
variables.description: reference to transport protocol of original R-URI

variables.name: $ou
variables.description: reference to request's original URI

variables.name: $oU
variables.description: reference to username in request's original URI

variables.name: $param()
variables.description: retrieves the parameters of the route. The index can be an integer, or a pseudo-variable (index starts at 1).

variables.name: $pd
variables.description: reference to domain in request's P-Preferred-Identity header URI (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $pn
variables.description: reference to Display Name in request's P-Preferred-Identity header (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $pp
variables.description: reference to process id (pid)

variables.name: $pU
variables.description: reference to user in request's P-Preferred-Identity header URI (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $pu
variables.description: reference to URI in request's P-Preferred-Identity header (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $rd
variables.description: reference to domain in request's URI

variables.name: $rb
variables.description: reference to the body or a body part of the SIP message

variables.name: $rc
variables.description: reference to returned code by last invoked function

variables.name: $re
variables.description: reference to Remote-Party-ID header URI

variables.name: $rm
variables.description: reference to request's method

variables.name: $rp
variables.description: reference to port of R-URI

variables.name: $rP
variables.description: reference to transport protocol of R-URI

variables.name: $rr
variables.description: reference to reply's reason

variables.name: $rs
variables.description: reference to reply's status

variables.name: $rt
variables.description: reference to URI of refer-to header

variables.name: $ru
variables.description: reference to request's URI

variables.name: $rU
variables.description: reference to username in request's URI

variables.name: $ru_q
variables.description: reference to q value of the R-URI

variables.name: $si
variables.description: reference to IP source address of the message

variables.name: $socket_in
variables.description: read-only variable to get the description (proto:ip:port format) of the inbound socket (used for receiving the message).

subfields.name: ip
subfields.description: the IP part of the socket

subfields.name: port
subfields.description: the port part of the socket

subfields.name: proto
subfields.description: the name of the protocol of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_ip
subfields.description: the advertised IP part of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_port
subfields.description: the advertised part part of the socket

subfields.name: tag
subfields.description: the socket internal tag/alias

subfields.name: anycast
subfields.description: if the socket uses an anycast IP or not

subfields.name: af
subfields.description: the address family of the socket's IP

variables.name: $socket_out
variables.description: read-write variable for reading or changing the outbound socket of the message.

subfields.name: ip
subfields.description: the IP part of the socket

subfields.name: port
subfields.description: the port part of the socket

subfields.name: proto
subfields.description: the name of the protocol of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_ip
subfields.description: the advertised IP part of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_port
subfields.description: the advertised part part of the socket

subfields.name: tag
subfields.description: the socket internal tag/alias

subfields.name: anycast
subfields.description: if the socket uses an anycast IP or not

subfields.name: af
subfields.description: the address family of the socket's IP

variables.name: $sp
variables.description: reference to the source port of the message

variables.name: $td
variables.description: reference to domain in URI of 'To' header

variables.name: $tn
variables.description: reference to display name of 'To' header

variables.name: $tt
variables.description: reference to tag parameter of 'To' header

variables.name: $tu
variables.description: reference to URI of 'To' header

variables.name: $tU
variables.description: reference to username in URI of 'To' header

variables.name: $time()
variables.description: returns the string formatted time according to UNIX date

variables.name: $T_branch_idx
variables.description: the index (starting with 1 for the first branch) of the branch for which is executed the branch_route[].

variables.name: $Tf
variables.description: reference string formatted time

variables.name: $Ts
variables.description: reference to current unix time stamp in seconds

variables.name: $Tsm
variables.description: reference to current microseconds of the current second

variables.name: $TS
variables.description: reference to startup unix time stamp

variables.name: $ua
variables.description: reference to user agent header field

variables.name: $hdr()
variables.description: represents the body of the N-th header identified by 'name'.

variables.name: $route
variables.description: Access route names of the current route call stack.

variables.name: $route.type
variables.description: Access the type of the current route. May be indexed, using positive or negative indexes.

variables.name: $route.name
variables.description: Access the name of the current route. May be indexed, using positive or negative indexes.

variables.name: $cfg_line
variables.description: Holds the current line from the script of the action being executed, useful for logging purposes

variables.name: $cfg_file
variables.description: Holds the current name of the cfg file being executed, useful when using multiple scripts via the include statement

variables.name: $xlog_level
variables.description: allows to set /reset the xlog() logging level on per-process bases.

examples.code:
xlog("current verbosity is $xlog_level \n");
$xlog_level = L_DBG; # force local xlogging limit to DBG
...
(set of xlogs)
...
$xlog_level = NULL;  # reset to initial value
